purpose: Teach: 閉会/ゲン/ヘルス/賜り/設問/緊密/同点/勧める

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: 創業祭の閉会の挨拶、私、心を込めて、お話、するからな、社員、皆、覚悟して、聞いてくれ、本当に、感謝の言葉、伝えたい、絶対、本当に。
lines.en: I'm going to give the closing address for the founding festival, and I want you all to listen carefully. I'm going to speak with all my heart—I truly want to convey my gratitude to every one of you.
lines.style: Measured and deliberate. Opens with quiet authority. Each phrase lands with intention, not rushed. The pauses are genuine—he's not performing gravity, he carries it. His voice settles lower at the end, a statement that asks for real attention.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: はい。創業以来、ゲン担ぎ、続けてきた、お父さんの代から、伝わる、伝統的な、習慣、続けてまいります、本当に、絶対、引き継ぎます、いつまでも。
lines.en: Yes, sir. Since our founding, we've carried on the traditions my father passed down—the good-luck practices, the customs. We will continue to inherit them, always. Truly.
lines.style: Respectful but not stiff. Measured delivery, each commitment stated plainly. There's warmth underneath the formality—not distancing himself from what he's saying, but honoring the weight of it. Slightly slower pace on the final affirmation.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: ヘルスケア事業、本気で、検討するか、社員の健康、第一に、考える企業、目指したい、本当に、絶対、頑張れ、本当に、頼んだぞ、社員、皆。
lines.en: Are we seriously going to look into a healthcare initiative? I want this company to put employee wellness first. I'm counting on all of you to make this happen.
lines.style: Direct and expectant. Opens with a question that's almost rhetorical—he's not asking for doubt. The tone shifts to command without becoming harsh: this is both invitation and instruction. Firm on 'first' and 'counting on you.' Not angry, but unambiguous.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: はい。お客様からの、お言葉、本当に、賜り、社員、皆、励みに、いたしております、本当に、感謝、申し上げます、お客様、皆様に、ですね、いつも、本当に。
lines.en: Yes. We've been truly fortunate to receive such kind words from our customers, and the whole team draws strength from that. I want to express our deep gratitude to all of them. We're always grateful, always.
lines.style: Warm and genuine. Opens with quiet acceptance, not defensive. The middle section flows with modest pride—he's sharing good news. The final repetition of gratitude isn't mechanical; it's him underscoring what matters. Steady breath, no rushing.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: 新人研修の設問、若手の発想、活かしたものに、変えていけ、固定した、ものでは、進歩、ないぞ、本当に、頼んだぞ、絶対、これは、本当に、絶対だ。
lines.en: The new-hire training questions—I want you to redesign them using the fresh ideas from our younger staff. We can't keep doing things the old way and expect to improve. This is non-negotiable.
lines.style: Instructive and firm. Opens with a clear directive. The tone carries conviction—he's not debating whether this is necessary. The final statement drops lower, more absolute. No room for passive compliance; he wants active change. Almost stern, but grounded in genuine belief.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: はい。お得意様との、緊密な、関係、社員、皆、心がけております、社長、本当に、引き続き、頑張ってまいります、絶対、頼りに、なる関係、築きます。
lines.en: Yes, sir. We're working hard to maintain close relationships with our valued clients. The entire team keeps this at the forefront of what we do. We're committed to building partnerships that you can truly rely on.
lines.style: Earnest and direct. Flows with professional composure but carries personal commitment. Not rote—he means each part. Opens with acceptance, builds through the middle with steady confidence, and lands the final promise as something he's willing to answer for. Measured pace, clear articulation.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: 競合と、シェア、同点、争う段階だ、当社、攻めの姿勢、絶対、見せていけ、社員、本気で、頑張れ、本当に、頼んだぞ、これは、最終決戦だ、本気。
lines.en: We're in a tie with our competitors right now, fighting for the same market share. I need this company to show an aggressive stance—all of you, seriously. This is our final chance. Don't hold back.
lines.style: Intense and urgent. Opens low and direct—sets the stakes immediately. Builds with clear focus and controlled intensity; this isn't shouting, it's certainty. The final words land harder: 'final chance' and 'don't hold back' are not suggestions. Breathing is tight, purposeful.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: はい。お客様に、当社製品、自信を持って、勧める社員、増やしていきたいですね、社長、本当に、若手、育てて、いきたいです、本気で、頼みます、本当に。
lines.en: Yes, sir. We want to increase the number of staff who can confidently recommend our products to customers. I'd like to invest in developing our younger people—truly, I'm asking for your support in making that happen.
lines.style: Earnest and direct, with a note of personal request. Opens with acceptance, then shifts into his own vision—he's not just reporting, he's proposing. The middle section carries conviction about the young staff's potential. Ends with genuine asking; his voice softens slightly on 'I'm asking,' showing he means the collaboration. Not presuming, inviting.
